gold.text: The user interface designer presented a prototype and slides covering joint work with the industrial designer.
The prototype had a wooden ergonomic case with customizable colour/backing, basic controls and voice control, plus an LCD in the flip panel provisionally subject to cost.

The project manager's EUR 9.95 estimate excluded an LCD price. Marketing estimated EUR 2-3 extra for the display, putting production near or above the EUR 12.50 allowance; wider promotion and transport costs also remained a concern.
The project manager planned to seek lower production costs from vendors and discuss cost reductions with management.
Marketing questioned whether the company could obtain enough market share and profit, modeling a EUR 50 selling price and EUR 25 per-unit margin.
The industrial designer proposed online promotion/ordering and direct shipping, with Amazon or eBay mentioned as possible channels; the team received the idea positively.
The user interface designer challenged the lack of redesign time after user testing. The project manager directed the team to freeze the current basic design and use feedback for a second generation.
Participants proposed aligning a user-tested launch with a sports event or a DVD promotion, and the project manager agreed to take the promotion idea to management.
The project manager will negotiate with vendors for lower production costs and discuss cost reductions with management.
The project manager will seek management support for a promotional campaign associated with a sports event or DVD release.
Ed, the marketing expert, is to take over follow-up once production is over.
Undertake user/product evaluation and market tests after real prototype units become available.
Include the LCD in the prototype provisionally; it can be removed if the additional cost is unacceptable.
Pursue vendor negotiation and management discussion to reduce production costs.
Pursue a promotional/launch association with a major sports event or a DVD release, subject to management support; no specific event, partner or date was fixed.

The project manager directed that the basic design be frozen for the first release, with customer feedback reserved for a possible second generation; the user interface designer continued to object to the testing/redesign risk.
Defer product/user evaluation until real prototype units are available, and begin full production/launch only after evaluation and technical/management approval.
The LCD was unpriced in the EUR 9.95 total, and its estimated extra cost left production near or above the EUR 12.50 allowance. Marketing also questioned the profit and market-share assumptions.

Place the microphone on the side so voice control remains accessible with the flip cover closed; detailed circuit-board placement was not specified.
Consider online ordering and direct shipping for the customizable product, with Amazon or eBay as possible channels.
The industrial designer and user interface designer completed and presented the jointly prepared prototype/model requested in meeting c.
